svg.title: The Conversion Waterfall That Exposes Acquisition Leakage
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-nested-claimant-quality-cohorts; chart type: funnel; title: The Conversion Waterfall That Exposes Acquisition Leakage; subtitle: A single illustrative annual cohort, with no entrants added between stages.; chapter number: 6; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Illustrative mature-cohort counts are 1,200, 480, 336, 252, and 210. Each stage is a strict subset of its predecessor. The final count identifies files associated with paid service invoices; it is not a count of per-case commissions or settlements.; caption: Conversions are 40.0%, 70.0%, 75.0%, and 83.33% sequentially; 17.5% of raw inquiries reach the final cohort. Annual Base revenue remains $705,000 from contracted services, not 210 multiplied by a claimant bounty.; stages: label: Raw inquiry cohort; value: 1,200 inquiries enter the same annual measurement cohort; numeric value: 1200.0; detail: Illustratively remove 180 duplicate or synthetic inquiries and 540 additional inquiries lacking eligibility, contact, or counsel acceptance before retainer completion. Retain mutually exclusive disposition codes so losses reconcile.; label: Signed retainer cohort; value: 480 retained claimants represent 40.0% of raw inquiries; numeric value: 480.0; detail: Counsel signs only after representation checks. At a fixed 540 other exclusions, increasing duplicate or synthetic losses from 180 to 240 reduces retained claimants to 420 before downstream attrition.; label: Usable proof cohort; value: 336 usable record packets represent 70.0% of retainers; numeric value: 336.0; detail: Reject 144 packets for absent exposure, incompatible dates, missing diagnosis support, or unusable records. The Base retrieval and triage pool is $66,000, equal to $137.50 per retained claimant or $196.43 per usable packet. At 60.0% usability, 288 packets cost $229.17 each.; label: Accepted case cohort; value: 252 accepted files represent 75.0% of usable packets; numeric value: 252.0; detail: Remove 84 files with unresolved firm-defined deficiencies. Define a 30-day contractual service-defect replacement window and charge actual rework to its responsible cost pool. If acceptance falls to 60.0%, expect about 202 files; do not represent rounding as an additional claimant.; label: Collected service cohort; value: 210 files associate with cleared vendor service invoices; numeric value: 210.0; detail: The remaining 42 accepted files associate with invoices still unpaid at the cohort cutoff. Cash status does not reverse properly recognized revenue automatically. Model a 60-day delay on one $58,750 monthly service invoice as a $58,750 working-capital exposure, not lost settlement value.

text.title: The Conversion Waterfall That Exposes Acquisition Leakage
text.tspan: The Conversion Waterfall That Exposes Acquisition Leakage

circle.title: label: Raw inquiry cohort; value: 1,200 inquiries enter the same annual measurement cohort; numeric value: 1200.0; detail: Illustratively remove 180 duplicate or synthetic inquiries and 540 additional inquiries lacking eligibility, contact, or counsel acceptance before retainer completion. Retain mutually exclusive disposition codes so losses reconcile.

label: Signed retainer cohort; value: 480 retained claimants represent 40.0% of raw inquiries; numeric value: 480.0; detail: Counsel signs only after representation checks. At a fixed 540 other exclusions, increasing duplicate or synthetic losses from 180 to 240 reduces retained claimants to 420 before downstream attrition.

label: Usable proof cohort; value: 336 usable record packets represent 70.0% of retainers; numeric value: 336.0; detail: Reject 144 packets for absent exposure, incompatible dates, missing diagnosis support, or unusable records. The Base retrieval and triage pool is $66,000, equal to $137.50 per retained claimant or $196.43 per usable packet. At 60.0% usability, 288 packets cost $229.17 each.

label: Accepted case cohort; value: 252 accepted files represent 75.0% of usable packets; numeric value: 252.0; detail: Remove 84 files with unresolved firm-defined deficiencies. Define a 30-day contractual service-defect replacement window and charge actual rework to its responsible cost pool. If acceptance falls to 60.0%, expect about 202 files; do not represent rounding as an additional claimant.

label: Collected service cohort; value: 210 files associate with cleared vendor service invoices; numeric value: 210.0; detail: The remaining 42 accepted files associate with invoices still unpaid at the cohort cutoff. Cash status does not reverse properly recognized revenue automatically. Model a 60-day delay on one $58,750 monthly service invoice as a $58,750 working-capital exposure, not lost settlement value.

text.title: Assumptions: Illustrative mature-cohort counts are 1,200, 480, 336, 252, and 210. Each stage is a strict subset of its predecessor. The final count identifies files associated with paid service invoices; it is not a count of per-case commissions or settlements.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Illustrative mature-cohort counts are 1,200, 480, 336, 252, and 210. Each stage is a strict subset of its predecessor.
The final count identifies files associated with paid service invoices; it is not a count of per-case commissions or settlements.

text.title: Stage widths/positions share a zero baseline; negative counts are unavailable.
